subject: Trouble with constructing a Genotype Accumulation Curve

messages.author: d8a8462b1ac35546
messages.subject: Trouble with constructing a Genotype Accumulation Curve
parts:
Dear All

I am quite new to R programming as well as using the package, "poppr". I have a dataset of 10 loci from 58 individuals from 3 populations which I have imported to RStudio as an xlsx file. I used the same command as the one for the dataset example of nancycats which reads as nan-geno <- genotype_curve(nancycats) from the paper "Produce a genotype accumulation curve" by Zhian N. Kamvar,  just with my information substitued in the command line. However, RStudio generated an output error, saying that the file has to be in genind or loci object. I then used the command provided by RStudio to generate a genind object of my file. I did manage to do that, however, the genind object generated could not be used to create the genotype curve since no data frame was generated under the optional content and it read as:
 //optional content
-empty-
This implies that when I run the command for the genotype accumulation curve, I received the same error output as before that the file has to be in genind or loci object, even though I did converted it into genind object.
Now I am wondering, where could I have made the mistake. Could it be that I did not convert me xlsx file into csv before the import or could it be that I only used the columns of the loci? However, I did troubleshoot to check and I imported the entire dataset with population names, sample codes, etc and got an error when I tried to convert it into genind. 
I would really appreciate your assistance on this and I thank you wholeheartedly in advance. 

Kindest regards
Martin

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Trouble with constructing a Genotype Accumulation Curve
parts:
Hello,

It is difficult to give you any recommendations based on your description without knowing the structure of your data. You can read in FSTAT, Gentix, GenePop, STRUCTURE, and GenAlEx files into poppr and I would recommend reading the data import section of the manual. If your data is formatted in another format (e.g. a spreadsheet with one row per individual and one column per locus as demonstrated in the Getting to know adegenet's genind object section of the manual, then you will want ot use the df2genind function.

Best,
Zhian
